record.paper_title: Open questions regarding the arrow of time
record.context_brief: Black holes, singularities, and information loss
record.original_question: In the quantum-gravitational treatment of black holes, should one impose a time-symmetric Weyl-tensor condition on all spacelike singularities, and would doing so eliminate genuine black-hole interiors, horizons, or information loss? Because the black-hole interior is causally inaccessible and quantum gravity no longer sharply distinguishes past from future singularities, the unresolved issue is whether a symmetric singularity condition is the correct way to understand black-hole entropy and avoid the information-loss paradox.

evidence.quote: This leaves much freedom for the unknowable physics inside. In particular, quantum gravity does not allow distinguishing between past and future singularities any more (see below).

Therefore, one can only postulate a Weyl tensor condition on all space-like singularities. Such a time-symmetric condition is not only compatible with all observations – it may even prevent black hole interiors and horizons to form (thus avoiding any genuine information loss paradox).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In a quantum-gravitational treatment of gravitational collapse, consider Penrose's Weyl curvature hypothesis, which in its original form requires the Weyl conformal tensor C_{abcd} of the spacetime metric to vanish (or be suitably bounded) at past spacelike singularities, thereby selecting a low-entropy initial state and providing a geometric origin for the thermodynamic arrow of time. In a regime where quantum gravity is taken to remove any sharp distinction between past-type and future-type spacelike singularities, one is led to consider a time-symmetric variant of this hypothesis: impose the same Weyl-tensor vanishing condition on every spacelike singularity of the spacetime, regardless of its temporal orientation.

Determine whether the following can be established:

(a) Imposing such a time-symmetric Weyl-tensor condition on all spacelike singularities is consistent with the standard formulation of black-hole thermodynamics (in particular with the area law for black-hole entropy and with the generalized second law), and is compatible with all current observational constraints on gravitational collapse and cosmology.

(b) Under this condition, no causally disconnected black-hole interior region and no event horizon can form in any classical or semiclassical solution describing gravitational collapse; equivalently, the symmetric Weyl condition forces the global causal structure to lack a true black-hole region in the sense of Hawking and Ellis.

(c) Consequently, the information-loss paradox associated with evaporating black holes does not arise, because the would-be interior and horizon are excluded by (b).

Either prove (a)–(c) within a precise framework for semiclassical or quantum gravity, or exhibit an obstruction (for example a spacetime satisfying the symmetric Weyl condition that nevertheless contains a genuine event horizon and causally hidden interior).
artifact.category_tag: Weyl curvature hypothesis and black-hole singularities
artifact.status_search_result: The Weyl curvature hypothesis remains a conjectural proposal of Penrose, with no accepted proof or refutation. Recent work (e.g. 2025 preprints on conservative resolutions of the singularity problem, and Weyl-invariant dilaton-gravity models replacing singularities by baby universes) explores related time-symmetric scenarios, but no consensus exists on whether a symmetric Weyl condition prevents horizon/interior formation or resolves information loss. The question is therefore considered open.

status_evidence.title: Weyl curvature hypothesis - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Penrose's hypothesis remains a proposal aimed at explaining the thermodynamic arrow of time via geometric constraints on initial singularities; its extension and proof status are unresolved.
status_evidence.claim: The Weyl curvature hypothesis is an open conjecture without an established proof.

status_evidence.title: A Conservative Solution to the Singularity Problem in Classical GR
status_evidence.snippet: Recent theoretical work proposes that no information is lost in scenarios where the singularity is replaced by a bubble manifold with vanishing Weyl curvature.
status_evidence.claim: Active recent research continues to explore Weyl-condition–based resolutions of singularities and information loss, indicating the question is open.

status_evidence.title: Aspects of Semiclassical Black Holes: Development and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of unresolved problems in semiclassical black-hole physics, including information loss.
status_evidence.claim: The information-loss paradox and the structure of black-hole interiors remain open in semiclassical/quantum gravity.
